newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Argos held share, Q4 sales slip.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Argos held share, Q4 sales slip.

text.p: British retailer Argos Plc said on Monday weakness in three of its key markets -- toys, small electricals and jewellery -- in the final quarter of 1996 were to blame for a slowdown in sales growth, although it had held on to market share.

Finance director Bob Stewart said in the final quarter of the year typically these three accounted for around 50 percent of sales. But in the final quarter the firm achieved just two percent growth in like for like sales in those three product areas. In the remaining 50 percent of the range Argos achieved eight percent like for like growth.

He said despite slower sales the group had managed to achieve "quite significant" market share improvements in toys and small electricals in the final quarter, and at least held on to market share in jewellery.
"The lower rate of like for like growth we had in the final quarter ...is due to those three markets rather than anything intrinsically wrong in the Argos offer," Stewart said in an interview.
